Month-by-month summary

"Avg duration" is total hours divided by complete days, so every complete day counts equally. "Avg of employee avgs" gives each employee equal weight, whatever their number of days. A full day means 9 hours or more, the shift length set in the biometric system. Click a row to filter the page to that month.

    How the numbers were worked out, and data issues found
    1. First check-in and last check-out only. For each employee and day, the earliest punch is the check-in and the latest is the check-out. Any punches in between are ignored. A working day runs from 5 AM to 5 AM, so someone leaving at 1:30 AM is counted on the day they arrived.
    2. Mis-paired punches were corrected. The biometric software often treats an evening punch (e.g. 20:32, really the check-out) as the start of a "night shift" and pairs it with the next day's arrival (e.g. 11:35), which shows up as a 15-hour day. About 800 records looked like this. They were split back into the correct days. Only 17 records looked like real late or night shifts (check-in after 6 PM, check-out by next morning, 10 hours or less). The 14 that ended before 5 AM are covered by the 5 AM rule, and the other 3 are kept whole as night shifts on their start date.
    3. "Days used" switch. "All complete days" counts every day with a check-in and check-out, including 674 days rebuilt from mis-paired records. "System records only" counts just the 2,113 days whose check-in and check-out come from one system record. The true average is likely between the two. Rebuilt days are tagged in the day-by-day list.
    4. Holidays. 14 Sep, 2 Oct and 9 Nov are marked as company holidays (the biometric software shows them as "Absent"). The few days people worked on a holiday stay in the averages, like Sunday work. Marking them changes the averages by at most 1 minute.
    5. Total hours = the sum of hours on complete days only. Days with a missing punch add nothing, so totals understate time actually spent.
    6. Status is not used to decide attendance. Any day with a punch counts as attended, including 175 days the software marks "Absent" because the hours were short. Two different employees are both named Aman Kumar, so use the employee code to tell them apart.
    7. The software's own "Duration" column was not used. On "No OutPunch" days it fills in hours up to the shift end, and on mis-paired days it caps them at 9:00 plus overtime, so it overstates both.
    8. A day counts toward averages only if it has a check-in and a check-out 1 to 16 hours apart. Days with one punch, or with two punches less than an hour apart (usually a double tap), are listed in the daily view but left out.
    9. November covers 1–21 Nov only. "All 3 months" averages are worked out from every complete day in the period, not by averaging the three monthly figures.
    10. Limitation: the report holds only one in and one out per system record, so some punches were already lost before this analysis. Exporting the raw punch log (the "Punch details" / "Log records" report from the biometric software) would recover the missing days.
    Source: AttendanceSummaryReport_1.xlsx (printed 23 Nov 2026). Report generated 23 Nov 2026.
